Asbestos Management Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Oakfield Lodge added to scope following a newly confirmed asbestos survey; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings.*

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages a confirmed asbestos register at a site where one applies. It now applies to Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge, following a newly confirmed asbestos survey at Oakfield Lodge; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings.

Policy statement

Riverside House, Moorland View and now Oakfield Lodge each maintain an asbestos register; any work disturbing a fabric surface must check the register first, preventing accidental disturbance of a material that presents a serious health risk if damaged.

Definitions

**Asbestos register** the documented record of confirmed or presumed asbestos-containing material within a building, based on a professional survey. **Fabric surface** a wall, ceiling, floor or other building surface that may conceal an asbestos-containing material behind or within it. **In-scope site** a site, now Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge, with a confirmed asbestos register under this procedure.

Roles and responsibilities

**Facilities** maintains the asbestos register for each in-scope site, now including Oakfield Lodge, and makes it available for consultation before any relevant work. **Any staff member or contractor** planning work that disturbs a fabric surface checks the register first via facilities. **The registered manager** at an in-scope site, including Oakfield Lodge's registered manager for the first time, ensures staff are aware the register exists and how to consult it.

1. Check the asbestos register via facilities before any work disturbing a fabric surface at Riverside House, Moorland View or Oakfield Lodge.
2. Never drill, cut or otherwise disturb a fabric surface at an in-scope site without confirming the register does not flag that specific location.
3. Stop work immediately and contact facilities if a suspected asbestos-containing material is discovered unexpectedly during work.
4. Brief a contractor working at an in-scope site on the asbestos register requirement as part of their site induction, now including a contractor working at Oakfield Lodge.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where work must proceed at an in-scope site with genuine urgency (for example, an emergency repair) and the register cannot be checked in time, a specialist assessment is arranged before work begins regardless of the urgency, since the health risk asbestos presents is too serious to bypass even under time pressure.

Local and regional variations

This procedure now applies to Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings without a confirmed asbestos register.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This procedure works alongside the Contractor Management Policy (governing the induction a contractor receives, including this requirement at an in-scope site) and the Health and Safety Policy (the wider framework this specific procedure sits within).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the newly extended scope. A contractor is booked to install a new shelf at Oakfield Lodge, work that under the previous version would not have required an asbestos register check at all. Under this version, following its newly confirmed survey, the same check-first standard now applies there as it always has at Riverside House and Moorland View, and the contractor checks the register via facilities before drilling.

Approval and review history

Appendix: the 72-hour clock at a glance

For quick reference: the clock starts when Alderbridge becomes aware of the breach, not when the
investigation concludes; internal reporting within 1 hour of discovery gives the Data Protection Lead the
maximum possible time within that window to investigate properly and, where required, notify the ICO with
a genuinely complete, accurate assessment rather than a rushed, incomplete one submitted only to beat
the deadline.

Breaches involving a third-party data processor

Where a breach occurs at a third-party data processor holding Alderbridge data (for example, a payroll
provider), the processor's own contractual obligation to notify Alderbridge without undue delay is relied on,
but the Data Protection Lead also proactively checks in with key processors periodically, since the 72-hour
clock for Alderbridge's own notification obligation still runs from when Alderbridge itself becomes aware,
which can be later than when the processor's own breach actually occurred if the processor is slow to tell
Alderbridge.

Extended frequently asked questions

**What if the breach involves a former employee's data rather than a current one?** The same procedure
applies in full; a former employee's data remains protected personal data for as long as Alderbridge holds
it. **Can a breach be assessed as low risk simply because the recipient is another Alderbridge employee
rather than an external party?** No — an internal misdirection can still be a genuine breach, particularly for
special category health data, and is assessed on the actual risk to the individual concerned, not assumed
low risk purely because it stayed within the organisation. **Is a physical break-in and theft of paper records
treated the same as a digital breach?** Yes — the same assessment and notification process applies
regardless of whether the compromised data was digital or physical.

DBS Renewal Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2024. Single substantive change: 'may register' becomes 'must
register' with the DBS Update Service.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how an enhanced DBS check is renewed for a staff member at Alderbridge Care
Group. It applies to every role requiring an enhanced DBS check.

Policy statement

Enhanced DBS checks are renewed every 3 years, and staff must register with the DBS Update Service to
allow faster status checks between renewals — this is now a requirement, not an option — supporting both
regulatory compliance and administrative efficiency.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the detailed criminal record and barring check required for a role involving
regulated activity with a vulnerable adult. **DBS Update Service** the subscription service allowing a DBS
certificate's status to be checked online rather than a fresh application, saving time on onward checks,
registration with which is now mandatory. **Renewal cycle** the 3-year interval at which a full check is
renewed.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** tracks every staff member's DBS renewal date and DBS Update Service registration, notifying the
registered manager 8 weeks before expiry. **The registered manager** ensures the renewal application is
submitted in good time and confirms DBS Update Service registration for every staff member requiring an
enhanced check. **The staff member** completes the renewal application promptly when asked and must
register with the DBS Update Service.

1. Renew an enhanced DBS check every 3 years for every role requiring one.

2. HR notifies the registered manager 8 weeks before a certificate is due to expire, allowing time for the
renewal application to be completed.

3. Staff must register with the DBS Update Service; this is now mandatory rather than optional as under
the previous version.

4. Restrict a staff member from regulated activity if their DBS check lapses without a renewal in progress,
until it is resolved.

Health and Safety Policy Full Manual

template, standardising what is presented to the Board each year across every area this manual covers.

Purpose and scope

This manual consolidates Alderbridge Care Group's full health and safety framework into a single
reference, now with a standardised annual reporting structure. It applies to every site and every member of
staff.

Policy statement

Alderbridge is committed to providing a safe working and living environment for staff, residents and
visitors, now with an annual health and safety report appendix standardising exactly what is presented to
the Board each year across every area this manual covers.

Definitions

**Risk assessment** the structured process of identifying a hazard and the control measure needed to
manage it. **Cyber and data risk** the area recognising that a system outage or data loss can directly
affect resident safety. **Annual health and safety report** the new standardised appendix, introduced in
this version, consolidating a year's data across every area into one comparable format.

Roles and responsibilities

**The Chief Executive** holds ultimate accountability for health and safety. **Each registered manager**
holds day-to-day responsibility for their site's compliance and contributes site-level data to the new annual
report. **Facilities, IT and the Quality Lead** jointly compile the new annual report using the standardised
template.

1. Complete and regularly review a risk assessment for every significant work activity and area.

2. Report a workplace incident or near miss through the Incident Reporting Policy.

3. Provide health and safety induction to every new staff member.

4. Check the asbestos register before any work disturbing a fabric surface at an in-scope site.

5. Follow the Lone Worker Devices Policy's device and check-in call requirement.

6. Know the manual fallback process for a critical system outage.

Site-by-site implementation notes

Riverside House and Moorland View each hold a comparatively small controlled drugs stock, reflecting
their smaller resident numbers, and their twice-daily stock checks are built into the existing morning and
evening medication rounds rather than run as a separate activity. Oakfield Lodge holds the largest
controlled drugs stock of the three North West and Midlands care homes and has, since 2025, additionally
logged its stock checks on a dedicated digital tablet mounted beside the cabinet, though the underlying
two-person, same-session signing rule is identical to every other site regardless of whether the register is
paper or digital. Harbour View and Meadow Court, both South West Region sites, coordinate their
twice-yearly Quality Lead audits so that a discrepancy pattern affecting the region generally, rather than
one site specifically, can be identified more easily. Willow Bank Community Service, as described under
Local and Regional Variations above, holds no controlled drugs stock on site at all, and its community-visit
witnessing model is the only variation this procedure permits from the otherwise universal two-person,
same-session standard.

every incident needing the registered manager personally, and extending it nationally in this version brings
that same reliability to every site, not only where it was first tested.

Where a new starter has made a valid application to the Home Office but is awaiting a decision, HR follows the specific guidance for this scenario, which may permit a start date to proceed with a follow-up check under that guidance's own terms; this remains the one defined route by which a start can proceed without the full check already complete.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the mandatory standard. A new care assistant's right-to-work document check is delayed by an administrative oversight, with their planned start date only two days away. Under this version, their start date is pushed back until the check is genuinely complete, whereas under the previous advisory wording there might have been more scope to let the start proceed while the check was finalised.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the wording changed from 'should' to 'must'?** A review found the advisory wording was sometimes read as allowing some flexibility on timing; the mandatory wording reflects the actual legal position more precisely, since there is no lawful flexibility here. **What happens if a check later reveals a document was not genuine?** This is escalated immediately and the employment situation reviewed under the relevant legal guidance.

Training and competency

HR staff completing right-to-work checks receive specific training on current acceptable document types and the online checking service, updated to reflect the mandatory standard.

Monitoring and compliance

HR reviews right-to-work check completion for every new starter as part of the wider new starter onboarding audit, with any gap now treated as a compliance breach rather than a missed best-practice target.

Record keeping and retention

Right-to-work check records and document copies are retained per the Records Retention Schedule and current Home Office guidance on retention periods.

Approval and review history

This overarching policy was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 March 2025, this version took effect 1 January 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in January 2027.

How the suite is kept up to date

A specific safeguarding procedure is reviewed on its own cycle, but any change is also checked against this overarching document, its appendices, and current terminology to confirm consistency across the whole suite.

Recognising self-neglect in practice

Self-neglect can present as declining personal hygiene support, an unwillingness to accept help with a deteriorating living space within the resident's own room, refusing food or fluids to a degree affecting health, or declining necessary medical treatment; staff are trained to notice these patterns and raise them, rather than dismissing them as simply 'the resident's choice' without the fuller Self-Neglect Guidance process being followed to properly weigh autonomy against risk.

Balancing autonomy and duty of care in self-neglect

The Self-Neglect Guidance requires a documented capacity assessment specific to the decision in question, since a resident may have capacity to decide about one aspect of their care while lacking it for another; where capacity is confirmed, the resident's own informed choice is respected and support is offered without being imposed, with the situation monitored and revisited periodically rather than treated as permanently settled.

Coordinating multi-agency information sharing in practice

Where a safeguarding concern involves another organisation, such as a domiciliary care provider a resident used before moving to Alderbridge, or a hospital involved in a recent admission, the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead coordinates what information is shared and requested, following the proportionality principle in the appendix rather than either withholding relevant information unhelpfully or sharing more than the situation genuinely requires.

Safeguarding Adults Board engagement

Alderbridge participates in the relevant local authority's Safeguarding Adults Board where a site's residents fall within that authority's area, contributing to multi-agency learning and receiving updates on local safeguarding priorities; the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead represents Alderbridge at this Board.

Closing word on new site openings

Any newly opened or acquired Alderbridge site completes a full COSHH register and assessment as part

Final closing note

This procedure is reviewed as a genuinely live document, expected to be corrected and clarified whenever
real experience shows a gap, rather than treated as finished once initially approved, and any member of
staff's own suggestion for improving it is genuinely welcomed by the Facilities Lead.

Closing word on new site openings

Any newly opened or acquired Alderbridge site completes a full COSHH register and assessment as part

Final closing note

This procedure is reviewed as a genuinely live document, expected to be corrected and clarified whenever
real experience shows a gap, rather than treated as finished once initially approved, and any member of

Approval and review history

This overarching policy was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 March 2025, this version took effect 1 January 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in January 2027.

How the suite is kept up to date

A specific safeguarding procedure is reviewed on its own cycle, but any change is also checked against this overarching document, its appendices, and current terminology to confirm consistency across the whole suite.

Recognising self-neglect in practice

Self-neglect can present as declining personal hygiene support, an unwillingness to accept help with a deteriorating living space within the resident's own room, refusing food or fluids to a degree affecting health, or declining necessary medical treatment; staff are trained to notice these patterns and raise them, rather than dismissing them as simply 'the resident's choice' without the fuller Self-Neglect Guidance process being followed to properly weigh autonomy against risk.

Balancing autonomy and duty of care in self-neglect

The Self-Neglect Guidance requires a documented capacity assessment specific to the decision in question, since a resident may have capacity to decide about one aspect of their care while lacking it for another; where capacity is confirmed, the resident's own informed choice is respected and support is offered without being imposed, with the situation monitored and revisited periodically rather than treated as permanently settled.

Coordinating multi-agency information sharing in practice

Where a safeguarding concern involves another organisation, such as a domiciliary care provider a resident used before moving to Alderbridge, or a hospital involved in a recent admission, the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead coordinates what information is shared and requested, following the proportionality principle in the appendix rather than either withholding re

4. No employee may start work without this check having been completed and recorded; this is now an absolute requirement, a tightening from the previous version's advisory wording.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a new starter has made a valid application to the Home Office but is awaiting a decision, HR follows the specific guidance for this scenario, which may permit a start date to proceed with a follow-up check under that guidance's own terms; this remains the one defined route by which a start can proceed without the full check already complete.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This procedure works alongside the Safer Recruitment Guidance (the wider pre-employment check framework this sits within) and the DBS Renewal Procedure (a parallel pre-employment and ongoing check).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the mandatory standard. A new care assistant's right-to-work document check is delayed by an administrative oversight, with their planned start date only two days away. Under this version, their start date is pushed back until the check is genuinely complete, whereas under the previous advisory wording there might have been more scope to let the start proceed while the check was finalised.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the wording changed from 'should' to 'must'?** A review found the advisory wording was sometimes read as allowing some flexibility on timing; the mandatory wording reflects the actual legal position more precisely, since there is no lawful flexibility here. **What happens if a check later reveals a document was not genuine?** This is escalated immediately and the employment situation reviewed under the relevant legal guidance.

This manual was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 September 2023, this version took effect 1

Working at height and confined spaces

A low-level task follows the Working at Height Guidance's approved step stool standard, while any
genuinely higher task or a confined space task is never attempted by site staff, both now captured within

Every item of portable electrical equipment is subject to a periodic portable appliance test, with test

DBS Renewal Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2024. Single substantive change: 'may register' becomes 'must
register' with the DBS Update Service.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how an enhanced DBS check is renewed for a staff member at Alderbridge Care
Group. It applies to every role requiring an enhanced DBS check.

Policy statement

Enhanced DBS checks are renewed every 3 years, and staff must register with the DBS Update Service to
allow faster status checks between renewals — this is now a requirement, not an option — supporting both
regulatory compliance and administrative efficiency.

Definitions

**Enhanced DBS check** the detailed criminal record and barring check required for a role involving
regulated activity with a vulnerable adult. **DBS Update Service** the subscription service allowing a DBS
certificate's status to be checked online rather than a fresh application, saving time on onward checks,
registration with which is now mandatory. **Renewal cycle** the 3-year interval at which a full check is
renewed.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** tracks every staff member's DBS renewal date and DBS Update Service registration, notifying the
registered manager 8 weeks before expiry. **The registered manager** ensures the renewal application is
submitted in good time and confirms DBS Update Service registration for every staff member requiring an
enhanced check. **The staff member** completes the renewal application promptly when asked and must
register with the DBS Update Service.

1. Renew an enhanced DBS check every 3 years for every role requiring one.

2. HR notifies the registered manager 8 weeks before a certificate is due to expire, allowing time for the
renewal application to be completed.

3. Staff must register with the DBS Update Service; this is now mandatory rather than optional as under
the previous version.

4. Restrict a staff member from regulated activity if their DBS check lapses without a renewal in progres
